Found and closed one real gap: `app/global-error.tsx` — the last-resort root error boundary (catches errors thrown by `layout.tsx` itself, which `app/error.tsx` can't reach) — had zero test coverage even though its sibling `app/error.tsx` was already tested. Added `tests/app/global-error.test.tsx` covering: no raw-error-message leakage, the "nothing was charged and no offer was lost" reassurance copy (the one line that matters most at this failure point), digest-present/absent reference line, `reset()` firing on retry, and that the real error still reaches `console.error` for diagnosis even though it's never rendered.

I checked `apple-icon.tsx` and `twitter-image.tsx` too, but both directly import `next/og`'s `ImageResponse` with no pure-component extraction the way `opengraph-image.tsx` has via `ShareCard.tsx` — the existing test's own comment explains why that split exists (satori/WASM isn't invokable from plain vitest). `twitter-image.tsx` just reuses `ShareCard` (already covered by `opengraph-image.test.tsx`); `apple-icon.tsx` is 20 lines of inline hardcoded-hex JSX with no separable logic. Writing a direct test for either would import the WASM-dependent `next/og` runtime and risk hanging/breaking vitest, contradicting the precedent the codebase already established — leaving both untested is consistent, not a gap.

That's it for my lane this round — no shared config touched, pure addition under `tests/app/`. Nothing left for the integrator to wire. The `npm install`-blocked caveat stands unchanged.
